audit.whatIsWrong: Neither Meditate nor Alpha Strike's untargetability appears anywhere on the page. Meditate is called nothing at all, and the only mention of Alpha Strike is 'Dodging Tangle-Barbs with Alpha timing'.
audit.why: Two flagged interactions decide this lane and both are actionable. Meditate is a channel that restores health and reduces damage taken — Tangle-Barbs or Pop Blossom cancels it outright, which is the difference between a poke lead that sticks and one he heals back every 10 seconds. Alpha Strike makes him untargetable mid-dash on a 20s cooldown that his basic attacks shorten, so a rotation spent into it lands on nothing.
audit.corrected: content.early now cancels Meditate with the root, and a new spikes[3] states the Alpha Strike untargetable window and its cooldown behaviour.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Neeko six of seven stages against a 47.18% win rate over 142 games — the packet chart instead reads Skill at first item, which is also what whys[5] on the same page says ('the duel evens out, so trade carefully').
audit.why: The first-item row contradicts its own why text, and 142 games is a large enough sample to take the packet chart seriously. The remaining rows are consistent: Neeko genuinely dominates a dashless melee pre-6, and Master Yi genuinely out-scales her.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] and content.late treat Highlander as an unanswerable dive button. Riot's text says it grants move and attack speed and makes him immune to all SLOWING effects — nothing more.
audit.why: Slow immunity is not CC immunity. Tangle-Barbs is a root and Pop Blossom is a knock-up-and-stun, and neither is a slow, so both still stop a Highlandered Master Yi cold. That converts the late game from 'never fight him' into a clear job: hold the root for the dive.
audit.corrected: whys[6] and content.late now state that Highlander only blanks slows, so the root still lands.
